processing: Typical of Darjeeling: orthodox black tea, withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, lighter in spring and fuller in summer.
harvest_season: As across Darjeeling, first flush in spring and second flush from around May to June, followed by monsoon and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Twisted Darjeeling leaf in mixed olive and brown, as usual for the region.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in spring, amber in summer.
taste_profile: Typical of high Darjeeling: floral and brisk in first flush, rounder and more fruity in second flush.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western-style, as for other Darjeeling. Use cooler water and a shorter steep for first flush.

vintage_note: As usual for Darjeeling, expect it sold by year and flush, often with a lot name or invoice number. Buy the latest harvest, and drink first flush within a year or two.
description:
Goomtee is a Kurseong garden with a good reputation among Darjeeling drinkers, spread over 110 planted hectares of a 225-hectare estate. Its slopes run from 3,000 to 6,000 feet, a wide span that means tea from different sections can differ.

Its neighbours include Jungpana and Sivitar. The making is the usual orthodox Darjeeling process, so season and section do most of the work.

First flush lots should be light and floral, and second flush fuller and fruitier. That is the regional pattern, not a note unique to this garden. Keep the water a little off the boil for spring tea.

The label to look for names the year and flush. With a garden like this, tasting two lots side by side tells you more than any grade letters.
history:
Henry Montgomery Lennox planted Goomtee in 1899. It was later managed by G. W. O'Brien, who had to sell it to the ruling Rana of Nepal after the Second World War.

In the mid-1950s it passed to co-owners, the Kejriwal family and Mahabir Prasad.
